surface: Visual-companion local HTTP/WebSocket server and helper that render agent-written HTML in a browser
boundary: server.cjs / helper.js HTML and DOM handling + loopback binding
attack_class: CLIENT-SIDE DOM-based XSS / DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC local server exposure
reason: This is a separate subsystem with its own HTML and DOM sinks and a local listener (createServer/WebSocket/innerHTML found by grep). It is outside the portal frontend boundary owned here, and no peer coverage ID names it.

boundary: repository-scoped VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET (job-level env) + host allowlist in scripts/check_deploy.mjs, script taken from the event/dispatched ref
reason: The same repo-scoped-secret, ref-unbound root cause applies to the Vercel bypass secret, and the deployment_status/free-text-URL handoff is a separate boundary that no listed coverage unit owns.

surface: Public GitHub issues/PR comments consumed by AI agent sessions that hold push and workflow-dispatch tools
boundary: untrusted issue text (public repo, docs/agents/issue-tracker.md, ready-for-agent label) ↔ agent authority to push branches and dispatch secret-bearing workflows
attack_class: AI-AND-LLM prompt injection into tool-holding agents
reason: This is the lower-trust input that would drive the agent along the secret-scope path above. It needs its own AI-AND-LLM unit; the listed peer agent-tooling unit covers plugin/hook supply chain, not issue-text injection.

surface: Disaster-recovery rebuild and restore paths: docs/backup_schema.sql replay, migrations replay order, scripts/restore_rest.mjs and the private dump restore
boundary: post-restore grants, RLS, default privileges, function placement (public vs audit/private) and Realtime publication
reason: Restored copies can re-create anon EXECUTE on diagnostics and table ACLs that the live hardening removed (baseline still grants them); no current coverage unit owns the restore lifecycle as an access-control boundary.

surface: anon Realtime postgres_changes subscriptions (supabase-js channel opened with the public anon key, 15 published tables)
boundary: Realtime per-tenant connection/channel quotas and per-subscriber RLS evaluation on each change
reason: This unit covers PostgREST statements bounded by statement_timeout and db_max_rows. Realtime subscriptions are a separate anon-reachable channel. Their cost (many sockets or subscriptions, each with server-side authorization work per WAL change) is bounded by Realtime quotas, not by the role timeouts reviewed here, and needs its own coverage.

boundary: deployment-SHA code checkout running with VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET in job env
attack_class: SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE / secret exposure across CI workloads
reason: deploy-smoke.yml:41 places the bypass secret in job env, and :62 checks out the default GITHUB_SHA. For deployment_status events that is the deployed commit, so the workflow definition and code come from whatever commit the Vercel app deployed. That can include fork or PR-head commits if Vercel fork protection or repo visibility allows it. Whether non-writer code can run with the secret depends on GitHub's deployment_status semantics and Vercel Git fork-protection settings. This is a CI trust-boundary question outside secret-hygiene/obvious-checklist scope and needs its own owner if no CI-secrets unit covers it.
